1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
The rain in Qingshi had been falling for three full days. Lin Xiaoyu's sister had gone to the capital in spring, and ever since, she'd been the only one looking after the small pharmacy in town.
After dark, she closed up the doors and windows, counted the day's earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when urgent knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man's voice: "Anyone there?"
Outside the door stood a young man drenched through, his left arm wrapped in a blood-soaked bandage. He said his name was Bai Yun, and that he was from the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need to have my wound bandaged," Bai Yun said in a low voice. "Can I pay you? Would three thousand five hundred wen be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oil paper from his chest. "This letter must reach Qingfeng before the eighteenth of May."
As she bandaged him, he said with a wry smile, "If my fiancée knew I was knocking on a young woman's door in the middle of the night, she'd be jealous for sure."
Lin Xiaoyu didn't take his money. "Early tomorrow morning," she said, "I'll take you up the mountain."
2: It was just dawn when the two of them set out. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket on her back, filled with dried provisions, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

On the mountainside, they met an old woodcutter, Zhou Dashan. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice. "Yesterday evening, three outsiders were asking about an injured young man at the town entrance."
"Xiaoyu, you should take the small path," Zhou Dashan said. "The main road isn't safe." Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The small path was narrow and slippery. Lin Xiaoyu walked ahead, planting each step firmly. Bai Yun followed behind, not saying a word.

At noon the rain stopped. The mist in the mountains slowly dispersed, and in the distance the roof of Qingfeng Temple came into view. Standing at the temple gate was a nun named Zhao Qiuyue, the guest attendant in charge of receiving visitors at the temple.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, examined the red seal on the flap, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting for this letter for two years."
Bai Yun said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come, help me repair the roof of the pharmacy." Bai Yun stayed at the temple.
In the evening, Lin Xiaoyu descended the mountain alone. When she arrived home, it was already dark. She lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
